name: How do you prove the pool was demolished for county records or tax assessment?

mainEntity.name: How do you prove the pool was demolished for county records, permit closeout, or tax assessment updates?
mainEntity.text: How do you prove the pool was demolished for county records, permit closeout, or tax assessment updates?

acceptedAnswer.text: After demolition, the most important paperwork is the record that the work was completed and approved. Depending on the city, that may include a final inspection sign-off, permit closeout record, contractor invoices, photos, and any soils or compaction reports. This documentation helps if the property record, insurance file, or tax assessment needs to reflect that the pool no longer exists. Some jurisdictions may also require the demolition permit as part of their assessment update process. Homeowners should save everything in one place and ask the contractor what proof the city expects at the end of the job. Missing final paperwork can create headaches years later when the property is sold or remodeled.
